cases.setup: Named identifiable case, explicit context/objective, no approval or register entry.
cases.expected: Analytical task accepts; no entry or occurrence is invented.

cases.setup: The same case is selected for an operational-register task with missing approval.
cases.expected: Core case retained; operational readiness is INCOMPLETE/UNKNOWN.

cases.setup: Operational request supplies explicit denied approval.
cases.expected: Core case retained; operational eligibility is NOT_ELIGIBLE, distinct from unknown.

cases.setup: Explicit linked entry records the selected case and supported approval is true.
cases.expected: Both selected analytical and local operational checks accept.

cases.setup: Approval is true but there is no register entry for this local task.
cases.expected: Case identity persists; the declared operational task is incomplete.

cases.setup: Case identifier is blank or malformed in a selected exchange record.
cases.expected: The selected named-identity profile rejects; raw input may remain staging.

cases.setup: Named case lacks explicit context required by the selected analysis task.
cases.expected: Task is incomplete; no case deletion/nonexistence claim. OWL may remain satisfiable using anonymous witnesses.

cases.setup: Named case lacks explicit objective required by the selected analysis task.
cases.expected: Task is incomplete; case identity is not contingent on operational approval.

cases.setup: Two distinct entries record one selected case.
cases.expected: Preserve one case and two entries; R-01 does not create a second case.

cases.setup: Two scoped case identities have equal labels; explicit distinctness can be supplied.
cases.expected: Do not merge by label or score. A HermiT consistency check uses explicit distinctness; it does not adjudicate real identity.

cases.setup: A register-entry identifier is reused as a case identifier.
cases.expected: Reject cross-family identity in the declared SQL/application contract; do not invent a new universal OWL disjointness axiom.

cases.setup: A scenario describes the selected item without an asserted occurrence.
cases.expected: Retain the scenario/case interpretation; assert no actual occurrence.

cases.setup: One case has unfavorable and favorable assertions under distinct objective/context references.
cases.expected: Retain the qualified assertions; no forced threat/opportunity partition or automatic case split.

cases.setup: Selected source cohorts contain old withheld decisions.
cases.expected: Every original byte/hash and withheld identity field remains unchanged. No real case admission is inferred.

cases.setup: Caller supplies no case target.
cases.expected: Reject an empty request rather than reporting vacuous acceptance.

cases.setup: Input tries to choose a permissive profile or supplies a schema/identity rewrite over reserved vocabulary.
cases.expected: Reject untrusted selector/schema injection before task validation.

cases.setup: The disposable case has no register entry.
cases.expected: Existing v_native_facts exports its case type; selected SQL and RDF identity/entry answers agree. This is not full context/approval persistence.

cases.setup: Deliberately omit the local approval requirement for an incomplete operational record.
cases.expected: The bad record becomes accepted and the fixed negative oracle detects the mutation.

cases.setup: A selected entry records a different case.
cases.expected: Reject the selected operational join; do not silently relink the entry or merge cases.

cases.setup: Generate the successor native/OWL from the explicit source delta.
cases.expected: 596 native elements and the B0 repair remain; logical OWL is isomorphic to the prior candidate after documentary annotations/version data are removed. New version/profile hashes are explicit.

limits: HermiT checks only the stated logical satisfiability/entailment cases; it does not establish semantic adequacy.
SHACL/application checks concern explicit selected-task input, not universal existence.
SQLite tests the bounded identity/history slice; PostgreSQL and full context/approval persistence are unclaimed.
External HTTP/live channel checks follow actual publication; no staged output is counted as deployed.
